a:r.a:t: Epinephrine and Glucagon Stimulate Breakdown of Glycogen

p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the cascade mechanism of epinephrine and glucagon action. This image has two halves, with myocyte on the left in pink and hepatocyte on the right in gray. In the middle is a large white box, where most of the action occurs. In the middle of the two boxes at the top, there is a pink box with "x molecules" inside. In the myocyte side, epinephrine is at the top and binds down to a green box, which is a piece of a larger image where the box would fit. From that image a dashed line goes down, then right to a green triangle in a circle. On the hepatocyte side, it begins with glycogen which binds to a triangle, which is part of a circle where the triangle would fit. From the circle, a dashed arrow goes down and left to a green triangle in a circle. Between these two green triangles is Gs alpha, which has a dashed arrow going down to another green triangle in a circle. Below that, ATP has a thick black arrow pointing right to cyclic AMP. Below that and to the right is a pink box with 20x molecules. Below the thick arrow, adenylyl cyclase is written in blue. Cyclic AMP has a wavy line pointing to another thick arrow pointing right going from inactive PKA to active PKA. Below that and to the right is a pink box with 10x molecules. A dashed wavy arrow goes from active PKA down to a green triangle in a circle, which also has another dashed arrow pointing right to it from [up arrow][Ca2+]. Below that inactive phosphorylase b kinase points to active phosphorylase b kinase with a thick black arrow. Below and to the right of that is a pink box with 100x molecules. A dashed arrow goes left and down from active phosphorylase b kinase to a green triangle in a circle just above another thick black arrow pointing right. That arrow goes from inactive glycogen phosphorylase b to active glycogen phosphorylase a. Below that and to the right is a pink box with 1,000x molecules. Below the arrow and to the left is [up arrow][AMP] is pointing right and down to a green triangle in a circle with a dashed arrow. Active glycogen phosphorylase a has a wavy dashed arrow pointing down to a green triangle in a circle, which sits above another thick arrow. This arrow points right from glycogen to glucose 1-phosphate. Below and to the right is a pink box with 10,000x molecules. From that box, an arrow goes left to myocyte box, pointing to glycolysis, which then points to muscle contraction. To the right, the arrow points to, in the hepatocyte section, glucose, which then points to blood glucose. Just below that and to the right is a pink box with 10,000x molecules.
